question: Tim had 184 dollars to invest. He tripled his investment money on the first day. He then added 27 dollars from his paycheck. His portfolio multiplied by 7 in value from a stock gain. He added 32 dollars more. His total assets multiplied by 4. How much money did Tim have at the end?

A library had 78 books initially in a donation box. In the morning, 12 books were damaged and removed. During the day, 74 books were added from a new donor. By afternoon, the books were tripled in their cataloging units. Then 56 books were processed. The final amount was reduced by 334 books sent to other libraries. He finally tripled the remainder for special counting. How many books were in the final count?

The gym had 219 members at the start of the month. The membership doubled with a promotion (multiplied by 2). Then 50 new members joined. The month saw 115 members leave. Another 7 members canceled. By month-end, 59 new members signed up. His friend who is a trainer had 100 members in his class (separate count). What was the final gym membership?

A bakery started the day with 61 cookies. In the morning, they baked 7 more. Then they made twice as many cookies (doubling the batch). They then divided the cookies into 4 equal packs. Each pack was then divided into 8 individual cookies. Finally, they multiplied by 5 for the display count. How many cookies were in the final display arrangement?

A farmer had 131 apples initially. In the morning harvest, he picked 60 more apples. Then he picked 45 additional apples in the afternoon. He packed them in groups of 4. He then created 3 crates from the groups. Each crate was multiplied by 8 for total storage capacity. How many apples could the storage system hold?

A shop had 22 items at opening. The inventory multiplied by 5 during morning restock. Then 64 items arrived from a supplier. The new total doubled. Finally, 44 more items arrived. How many items were in the shop at the end?

A child received 36 dollars from relatives. She spent 21 dollars on toys. She tripled her remaining money with a matching gift program. Then she received 50 dollars more. She multiplied her total by 5 for savings goal tracking. How many dollars in her savings goal was set?

A runner trained for a race that would take 3 hours. He started with 87 calories to burn. He divided his workout into thirds, burning 29 calories in each third. He then burned 5 times that amount during the main race. Unfortunately, 102 calories were lost due to measurement error. His final burn total decreased by 17 more. How many calories did he burn in total?

Lisa had 218 dollars in her checking account. In the morning, she deposited 6 dollars. At noon, she added 9 dollars more. By afternoon, she added 16 dollars. At that point, 204 dollars were withdrawn for bills. By evening, 25 dollars were removed for groceries. Her brother Mike had 150 dollars (kept in a separate account). What was Lisa's final account balance in dollars?

A garden started with 23 tomato plants. In the morning, 19 more were planted. By afternoon, 22 additional plants were added. Each plant would grow 5 tomatoes. Then 41 more tomatoes were harvested from other vines. How many tomatoes would be produced in total?

A production line started with 52 items per hour in the morning. By mid-morning, the rate multiplied by 7 (faster machines). By afternoon, it doubled to 7 times the doubled amount. Then 5 bonus items were added per hour. By evening, the hourly rate multiplied by 6. What was the final hourly production rate?

A factory had 166 workers. In the morning shift, the workforce multiplied by 6. At lunch, the crew was split equally in half. In the afternoon, they split again in thirds. By the evening, the group multiplied by 8. Finally, 423 workers left for the day. How many workers remained?

A restaurant served 223 customers at opening. By morning rush, 30 more arrived. The customer count then multiplied by 9 for peak lunch. By afternoon, 19 additional customers were seated. Evening brought 27 more. Finally, the count doubled for the night shift projection. After all this, how many customers did the restaurant project for the night?

A workshop had 91 participants in the morning. By afternoon, 12 left early. Then 23 joined from another session. The group multiplied by 5 for a group project. By evening, the number doubled. The final count was divided into 5 equal learning groups. How many people were in each group?

A store started with 160 items. In the morning, the count multiplied by 8. By afternoon, the inventory was split into 5 equal departments. Then 103 items were sold. By evening, 71 items arrived. What was the final inventory count?

An account had 203 dollars. By morning, 111 dollars were spent. The remaining amount was divided equally into 4 parts. Then 4 dollars were deducted from the total. By afternoon, 36 dollars were added. By evening, 13 dollars were withdrawn. Meanwhile, a related account had 50 dollars. How much was left in the account?

A project started with 89 hours of work. By morning, 34 hours were completed. The remaining hours multiplied by 8 for estimation. Then 218 hours were already accounted for. An additional 58 hours were subtracted. Finally, 20 more hours were removed as unnecessary. How many hours remained?

A class started with 102 students. In the morning, the enrollment multiplied by 6. By midday, this doubled by 5. By afternoon, another multiplication by 3. Then 70 more students were added for the evening session. His adjacent class had 95 students (separate). How many total did the class grow to?

A project budget started at 231 dollars. In the morning phase, 61 dollars were added. By midday, the budget multiplied by 6. By afternoon, it multiplied by 3 more. By evening, 4329 dollars were spent. How much remained in the budget?

A gym had 110 members initially. In the morning, membership multiplied by 5. By afternoon, 70 more joined. The total was then split into 4 training groups. By evening, 70 members left. How many remained in the gym?

A supply chain had 123 items at opening. In the morning, the count multiplied by 7. By midday, 28 items were used. The inventory multiplied by 7 for the afternoon count. By evening, 48 more items arrived. Finally, 3762 items were shipped out for distribution. How many items remained in stock?

A worker had 35 tasks to complete. In the morning, they started with 1 task left to assign. By mid-morning, the workload multiplied by 7. By noon, 14 tasks were completed. By afternoon, the remaining multiplied by 9. By evening, another multiplication by 5 occurred. His co-worker had similar tasks. How many tasks did the worker track?

A product started with 97 units. In the morning, production multiplied by 8. By afternoon, output multiplied by 4 more. Then 53 units were added from a shipment. By evening, 3030 units were removed for distribution. The count was measured in bundles of items. How many units remained in storage?

Marcus had 52 dollars on Monday. He earned 59 dollars from his job. He paid off 62 dollars in debt. He then spent 7 dollars on lunch. His money was quadrupled for his savings goal calculation. His roommate earned 80 dollars (separate account). What was Marcus's money worth in his savings plan?

An author had 196 pages written. In the morning, she added 16 pages. By afternoon, she added 75 more pages. Then 35 pages were removed for editing. She multiplied her final manuscript by 8 for the number of copies needed. How many pages would 8 copies total?
